description: A 2023 GeoHealth review by the Virginia Scientist-Community Interface and university co-authors of the health effects of natural gas pipeline compressor stations. Contents: the chemical pollutants compressor stations release, sometimes above national air quality standards, the health effects of those pollutants, evidence on local communities, including siting in rural areas with higher poverty or minority populations, and policy recommendations: more EPA and state air monitoring and data transparency, monitoring at compressor stations, free indoor air monitoring for nearby homes, tighter ambient standards that account for cumulative impacts, and community involvement. Pollutant concentrations shown in the paper come from EPA AirData monitors. Coverage: United States, drawing on published studies and monitor data. Format and access: open article. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: a narrative review that compiles evidence, not a new measurement dataset. Useful for choosing pollutants, exposure pathways and health end points in hazard exposure models of pipeline compressor sites. It relates to the [EI]3 infrastructure population dataset and the EIA compressor station report in the catalogue.
